games.title: Splitgate
games.note: Arena matches where you shoot portals onto walls to flank, peek and escape. Its 2021 console launch drew a sudden crowd.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six: Rogue Spear
games.note: The sequel to Rainbow Six. Valorant's director later named it, with Counter-Strike 1.6, as an influence.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon
games.note: Took Rainbow Six's careful squad tactics outdoors, into the forests and villages of a near-future Eastern Europe.

games.title: SWAT 4
games.note: A police tactics game whose score rewards arrests and following the rules of engagement over kills.

games.title: Ready or Not
games.note: Made by Irish studio VOID Interactive. Early access from 2021, full release in 2023, consoles in 2025.

games.title: Hell Let Loose
games.note: World War II battles with 50 players per side, funded on Kickstarter in 2017. Team17 bought the game in 2022.

games.title: Marvel Rivals
games.note: A free-to-play hero shooter with Marvel characters, team-up abilities and parts of maps you can destroy.

games.title: Concord
games.note: Taken offline about two weeks after its August 2024 launch, with every copy refunded. Sony then closed the studio.

games.title: Fortnite: Save the World
games.note: Announced in 2011 and released in early access in 2017. Players build forts and defend them against monster storms.

games.title: Minecraft
games.note: Started by Markus Persson in Stockholm in 2009. It became the best-selling video game of all time.

games.title: Dark Sector
games.note: Its hero throws a three-bladed glaive. The first, sci-fi concept was shelved and later revived as Warframe.

games.title: Warframe
games.note: Self-published as a free-to-play game after publishers rejected the idea. Players are Tenno, space ninjas in powered suits.

games.title: Tom Clancy's The Division
games.note: Made by Massive in Malmö on Ubisoft's Snowdrop engine. Set in a New York quarantined after a smallpox attack.

games.title: Helldivers
games.note: A top-down co-op shooter where friendly fire is always on, even from the airstrikes you call in.

games.title: Helldivers 2
games.note: A Stockholm studio's satirical co-op war. A real game master steers the shared galactic campaign for all players.

games.title: Dungeons & Dragons
games.note: The first commercial role-playing game, grown out of tabletop wargames in Lake Geneva, Wisconsin.

games.title: Drakar och Demoner
games.note: Sweden's best-known tabletop role-playing game. The name means Dragons and Demons.

games.title: Payday: The Heist
games.note: Four robbers in clown masks pull bank jobs while police assaults escalate. Made in Stockholm, designed by Ulf Andersson.

games.title: Payday 2
games.note: Supported with updates for about a decade, adding stealth routes and many new heists.

games.title: GTFO
games.note: A hard four-player horror shooter. It left early access in 2021, announced at The Game Awards.

games.title: Battlefield 2042
games.note: Swapped classes for named specialists on 128-player maps. Its rough launch shaped the plans for Battlefield 6.

links.took: Class-based team play; Jeff Kaplan said 'Team Fortress 2 was just mega' to him.
links.added: Heroes with unique abilities and ultimates, built for objective-based six-a-side matches.

src.t: Game Informer, Jeff Kaplan interview (Daniel Tack), Apr 2016

links.extra: Kaplan had played the original Team Fortress as a Quake mod.

links.took: Heroes as characters you get to know, from MOBAs such as Dota and League of Legends.
links.added: Kept it a shooter: Kaplan's team wanted MOBA-style heroes, not a MOBA.

src.t: Game Informer, Jeff Kaplan interview (Daniel Tack), Apr 2016

links.extra: Kaplan named DotA, Dota 2, League of Legends and Heroes of the Storm.

links.took: Overwatch popularized the hero shooter; each Apex Legend has a set of unique abilities.
links.added: Put heroes into a battle royale with Titanfall movement and a ping system.

links.took: Overwatch popularized ability-driven hero shooters; each Valorant Agent has signature skills.
links.added: One-life tactical rounds with a buy menu and a bomb to plant.
links.extra: Riot named Counter-Strike 1.6 and Rogue Spear as influences, not Overwatch.

links.took: Overwatch popularized the team hero shooter that Marvel Rivals is built around.
links.added: Marvel characters, team-up abilities between specific heroes, and destructible map sections.

links.took: Hero-shooter design; critics compared it with Overwatch, Apex Legends and Valorant.
links.added: A paid launch and a Guardians of the Galaxy-style crew; it closed within two weeks.
links.extra: Failing to stand out from those games was cited as a reason it shut down.

links.took: Red Storm's planning-heavy counter-terrorist shooting with one-shot kills.
links.added: More missions, weapons and online modes in the same careful style.

links.took: Tactical tension where one shot can kill; Joe Ziegler named R6 Rogue Spear an influence.
links.added: Agent abilities on top of precise gunplay, in free-to-play five-a-side rounds.

src.t: THESPIKE.GG, quoting Valorant director Joe Ziegler to Inquirer, Aug 2020

links.took: Creative ability use; Ziegler said the team drew on games like LoL and WoW.
links.added: Abilities that set up gunfights rather than replace them.

src.t: THESPIKE.GG, quoting Valorant director Joe Ziegler to Inquirer, Aug 2020

links.extra: Riot's own MOBA; Ziegler also named World of Warcraft.

links.took: Red Storm's realistic squad shooting, where a bullet or two kills.
links.added: Moved the squad from buildings to forests and villages, with two fireteams.

links.took: The series' core of careful, lethal team tactics, which Siege's new team returned to.
links.added: Destructible walls and floors, and attackers versus defenders on small maps.

src.t: Wikipedia: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege

links.extra: Siege replaced the cancelled Rainbow 6: Patriots.

links.took: Counter-Strike popularized five-a-side attack-and-defend rounds with no respawns.
links.added: Operators with gadgets, drones for scouting, and walls you reinforce or breach.

src.t: Wikipedia: Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Siege

links.extra: Critics compared Siege's esports scene favorably with Counter-Strike: Global Offensive.

links.took: Methodical police room-clearing, where arresting suspects beats shooting them.
links.added: Modern visuals, harsher scenarios and online co-op for up to five players.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls it a spiritual successor to Sierra's SWAT series; SWAT 4 is the best-known entry.

links.took: Squad popularized large realistic battles run by squad leaders, radios and supply lines.
links.added: World War II fronts, artillery, a commander role and 50-a-side matches.

links.took: Halo's gunplay; Ian Proulx said his team of Halo 1 to 3 fans took the best parts.
links.added: Portals you shoot onto walls, in free-to-play arena matches.

src.t: Xbox Wire, Ian Proulx (1047 Games), Oct 2021

links.extra: Proulx calls Halo 2 his favorite game of all time.

links.took: Portals: since playing Portal 2, Proulx had wondered how they would work in a shooter.
links.added: Portals as combat tools for flanking, peeking and escaping during fights.

src.t: Xbox Wire, Ian Proulx (1047 Games), Oct 2021

links.took: Fast arena multiplayer; Proulx named the older Halo games and Unreal Tournament alongside Portal.
links.added: Portal tricks layered on classic arena modes and map control.

links.took: Gathering and building; lead developer Lee Perry said Minecraft was 'an inspiration for sure'.
links.added: Building forts by day to defend against monster hordes, in a cartoon co-op shooter.
links.extra: Cliff Bleszinski announced it in December 2011 with the pitch: explore, scavenge, build and survive.

links.took: The engine, art, weapons and building system of Epic's co-op game.
links.added: A free 100-player battle royale where you build cover and ramps mid-fight.

links.took: PUBG popularized the 100-player battle royale with a shrinking circle.
links.added: 150 players, a Gulag duel for a second life, and cash to buy loadouts.

links.took: Stealth elements in the 2004 version, inspired by the Metal Gear Solid series.
links.added: A third-person action game built around throwing a returning three-bladed glaive.

links.took: Digital Extremes' original sci-fi vision for Dark Sector, revived with its ideas and assets.
links.added: A free-to-play co-op game about space ninjas, self-published in 2013.

links.took: Digital Extremes co-developed Unreal Tournament; early Dark Sector paired its action with a persistent online world.
links.added: Fast melee, parkour and ever-growing loot in a free-to-play live game.

links.took: Borderlands set the looter-shooter mold: gear with random stats and color-coded rarity.
links.added: A third-person cover shooter in quarantined New York, with player-versus-player Dark Zones.

links.took: Arrowhead's co-op war, with friendly fire always on and airstrikes you call in.
links.added: A third-person view and one shared galactic war run by a game master.

src.t: PlayStation Blog, how Arrowhead turned the twin-stick original into a PS5 sequel, Mar 2024

links.took: Tabletop role-playing's freedom and chaos; Johan Pilestedt says the game draws from D&D.
links.added: A real game master who steers the galactic war for every player.

links.took: Swedish role-playing sessions where, Pilestedt says, players always turn everything into farce.
links.added: Turned that farce into friendly-fire mishaps and a story that moves with the war.

src.t: Moviezine, Anders Eklöf (citing Pilestedt in PC Gamer and The New York Times), Dec 2024

links.took: Four-player co-op against waves of enemies, which Left 4 Dead revived.
links.added: Bank robberies with drills, hostages and escalating police assaults.

src.t: Game Developer, A Big Score: A Payday: The Heist analysis

links.extra: In 2012 the two games crossed over in Payday's free No Mercy heist.

links.took: Overkill's four-player heist shooting.
links.added: Stealth options, a job board of heists and years of updates.

links.took: Same lead: Ulf Andersson designed Payday at Overkill, then directed GTFO.
links.added: Hardcore four-player horror in dark complexes where noise wakes sleeping monsters.

links.took: Left 4 Dead popularized four-player co-op shooters against monster hordes.
links.added: Far harsher: scarce ammo, sleeping enemies, and teamwork needed to survive.

links.took: Digging through terrain; the team took inspiration from Minecraft and Left 4 Dead.
links.added: Four space dwarves mining fully destructible caves while holding off alien swarms.

links.took: Close-quarters destruction; producer Jeremy Chubb called Bad Company 2 a 'huge inspiration'.
links.added: Building-level destruction on modern maps, after 2042 was 'kind of missing' it.

links.took: A modern setting; creative director Thomas Andersson calls BF6 a spiritual successor to BF3 and BF4.
links.added: Made by four EA studios working together as Battlefield Studios.

links.took: The assault, engineer, support and recon classes of the BF3 and BF4 era.
links.added: New moves such as dragging a downed teammate to cover while reviving.
links.extra: Narrative director Emily Grace Buck called BF3 and BF4 the team's biggest touchstones.

links.took: DICE's large-scale combined-arms war.
links.added: 128-player maps, named specialists instead of classes, and extreme weather.

links.took: Lessons from 2042, which a producer said was ambitious but lacked 'the right feel'.
links.added: Returned to classic classes, tighter maps and close-quarters destruction.

links.took: Built as a mod for Battlefield 2 and its large combined-arms maps.
links.added: Realism, squad leaders and team logistics; it became a standalone game in 2015.

links.took: Battlefield 1942 popularized big team battles over capture points with vehicles.
links.added: Star Wars armies, starships and famous battles, made by Pandemic Studios.
links.extra: GameSpot compared its gameplay favorably with Battlefield 1942.

links.took: Collapsing buildings from DICE's Bad Company games, where Embark animation director Mikael Högström worked.
links.added: Server-side physics so whole buildings fall the same way for every player.
links.extra: The Ringer calls Bad Company 2's 'Destruction 2.0' the peak of that era.

links.took: Destructible environments; Embark's Mikael Högström calls Red Faction 'the staple of destruction'.
links.added: Destruction as the core of a game show about cashing out stolen money.
links.extra: The Ringer traces game destruction from Red Faction's Geo-Mod to The Finals.

links.took: A deadly televised game show as the setting; Embark named Smash TV an influence.
links.added: Teams fighting over cash in fully destructible arenas, with sponsors and commentators.
links.extra: Embark also named The Running Man, American Gladiators, The Hunger Games and Squid Game.

links.took: A $40 paid launch: Embark saw ARC Raiders as a double-A game like Helldivers 2.
links.added: Used that model for a PvPvE extraction shooter instead of free-to-play.

src.t: GamesBeat, Dean Takahashi (Patrick Söderlund interview), Dec 2025

links.extra: About pricing, not gameplay.

links.took: Bungie's original setting: the new game is set on Tau Ceti IV, 99 years later.
links.added: A PvP extraction shooter where crews of Runners loot the planet and try to escape.
links.extra: Released March 5, 2026; reviews were mostly positive but sales fell short of expectations.

links.took: Its director, Joe Ziegler, who earlier led Valorant at Riot Games.
links.added: Raids where dying means losing your gear, instead of round-based tactics.

src.t: THESPIKE.GG, Joe Ziegler as Valorant game director, 2020

links.extra: Ziegler shares the director credit with Del Chafe III.

links.took: Producer Hisashi Nogami named Perfect Dark; director Yusuke Amano played it heavily in college.
links.added: Shooting ink to claim turf and swimming through it as a squid.
links.extra: Nintendo Life doubted how much this shaped the game.

updates.why: Optional. Every later Battlefield has its own node and this one links to Battlefield Vietnam as its sequel, so it already acts as Battlefield 1942. If kept as a series node, its Project Reality link (a Battlefield 2 mod) is better served by battlefield-2 to project-reality, added in shooters-2.

updates.value: Made by a team of 14 at Digital Illusions (DICE) in Sweden, on the formula of Refraction Games' Codename Eagle.
updates.why: Wikipedia: Battlefield 1942, Development section. Only if the title update above is accepted.
Wikipedia: the 2004 Star Wars: Battlefront was developed by Pandemic Studios; DICE made the 2015 reboot. The catalog row also mixes the 2004 platforms with DICE and 2015.
